item.title: Semaglutide prescribing information to highlight rare vision loss risk
item.description: Yellow Card reports have prompted updated advice on the risk of nonarteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in patients using semaglutide.

item.title: UKMEC update: practices may need to review patients’ contraception, says GP
item.description: Practices will need to review some patients’ contraceptive prescriptions to ensure compliance with the recently updated UK Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, GP Dr Toni Hazell says in the MIMS Learning Clinical Update podcast.

item.title: Inhaler switching: one in 10 patients switch back without telling their GP, survey finds
item.description: One in 10 patients whose inhaler is switched subsequently switch back to their old inhaler without informing their GP, according to an Asthma + Lung UK survey.

item.title: Additional aspirin shortages reported
item.description: Aspirin gastro-resistant tablets are in limited supply following an increase in demand.

item.title: GPs to see medicine shortages ‘in real time’ this year
item.description: GPs will be able to access live information on drug shortages at the point of prescribing from this year, a health minister has said.

item.title: ‘Practice-changing’ analysis backs transdermal HRT for some women with amenorrhoea
item.description: Transdermal HRT is better than the combined oral contraceptive pill for improving bone mineral density in women with amenorrhoea due to anorexia or exercise, according to an ‘immediately practice-changing’ review and meta-analysis.

item.title: Antidepressant shortage reported
item.description: Clinicians are being asked to manage stocks of clomipramine 50mg capsules.

item.title: Anticonvulsant supply disruption warning
item.description: Supply of some strengths of phenobarbital tablets is disrupted.

item.title: First-line role of SGLT2 inhibitors in diabetes cemented in final NICE guidance
item.description: NICE now recommends SGLT2 inhibitors, as well as metformin, as first-line therapy for type II diabetes in final guidance published today.

item.title: Stopping antidepressants in pregnancy significantly increases risk of mental health emergency
item.description: In a recent study involving almost 4,000 pregnant women with depression/anxiety, discontinuation of antidepressants was associated with almost double the risk of mental health emergencies.
